# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Extract worklist constants, types and layout

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 1 of 7 extraction slices (leaf modules).

## Target outcome

The three leaf modules of the split exist, carry the module-level doc comments
required by parent AC6, and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports them from
its barrel position — no consumer or test change required.

## Scope (measured line ranges on the current `dev` tree)

| New module | Contents (current `worklist.ts` lines) | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.constants.ts` | Constants (164–224): `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`/`Stage`, `STAGE_MAP`, `PRIORITY_MAP`, `STAGE_COLORS`; `ANSI` (345–368); mouse timing `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` (3558–3592); any tooltip/chord tuning constants | ~170 |

| `worklist.layout.ts` | `MIN_META_SHARE`, `MAX_META_SHARE`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`, `computeDynamicLayout` (226–316), `getTermSize` (327–344) | ~130 |

`worklist.types.ts` **must be a leaf**: type-only declarations, no imports from
any other `worklist.*` module (parent AC4 — this is what keeps later modules
cycle-free).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `worklist.constants.ts`, `worklist.types.ts` and `worklist.layout.ts` exist,
   each ≤1,000 lines, each opening with a doc comment stating its single
   responsibility (AC6).
2. Provenance comments move with their code: the `// ── Constants ──`,
   `// ── /wl <stage> argument map (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G) ──`,
   `// ── /wl --priority <priority> map (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ──`,
   `// ── Metadata panel sizing ──`, `// ── Terminal helpers ──` banners and all
   inline work-item ids survive verbatim in the destination modules.
3. `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports the symbols in this slice that
   consumers actually use — `ANSI`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`, `Stage`,
   `TermSize`, `getTermSize`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`,
   `computeDynamicLayout`, `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`,
   `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`,
   `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`. **Internal** (declared in
   the new modules, exported from them for sibling use, but *not* re-exported by
   the barrel, because no external consumer imports them): `KeyAction`,
   `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`,
   `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ViewMode`, `MIN_META_SHARE`,
   `MAX_META_SHARE`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*
4. `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` is green: every baseline/consumer symbol still
   exported from `./worklist.js`, no worklist module imports the barrel at
   runtime, no new cycle, all modules ≤1,000 lines (AC4, AC1, AC2).
5. `tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) succeeds and the full
   `packages/herdr` suite passes with **no test-file changes** (AC3, AC9).
6. Documentation that names these symbols is updated to the new module paths:
   `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block around line 2345 and the
   `ANSI`/colour references), `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` (line 77) if the
   `formatItemLine` reference needs the new home (deferred there if format has
   not moved yet — record the deferral in a comment).
7. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 24 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,988 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
   → Owned by this slice: no test file is modified and the `packages/herdr` suite is green.
8. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
   → Owned by this slice: the guard's cycle gate reports no new circular import.
9. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
   → Owned by this slice: each module created here carries a responsibility doc comment and the moved provenance banners/comments are verbatim.

# Extract shared data-file push preamble helper

Refactor child of WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble
shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`). Its
sibling *Pin push-path policy divergence with tests* lands the behavioural tests
first; this child performs the dedupe and must leave those tests untouched and
green.

## Why

`gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
(rewrite) in `src/sync/push.ts` each carry a near-identical preamble:

1. cross-project guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`)
2. `refs/heads/` + `refs/tags/` safety guard
3. `git rev-parse --git-dir`
4. repo-root / repo-relative-path resolution (`getRepoRoot`,
   `getRepoRelativePath`, `path.resolve`)
5. data-file existence check
6. `withTempWorktree(...)`
7. `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`
8. `git add -f`
9. `git diff --cached`
10. `git commit`

A fix to any one of those steps must currently be made twice and can silently
drift.

## Desired change

One **private** helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name
`withDataFileInTempWorktree`) owns the preamble and delegates the
mode-specific tail to a callback:

- **Guard + resolve:** `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs rejection,
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` /
  `path.resolve()`, and the existence check.
- **Materialise:** `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, …, { forceOrphan })`,
  `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- **Commit**, then invoke the caller's `run(worktreePath, relativePath, …)` so
  each caller performs only its own push and post-push bookkeeping.

The four documented behavioural differences must stay **explicit options**, not
collapsed:

- `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op **without**
  invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing
  `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` message.
- `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` returns silently; `'throw'` raises
  `Worklog data file not found: <path>`.
- `forceOrphan: boolean` — `true` only for the rewrite path.
- `skipPrePushHint: boolean` — `true` only for the incremental path, so both
  guard messages stay byte-identical to today.

The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup (`listTrackedFiles` +
`git rm` + `git clean -fdx`) stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback — it
is mode-specific, not preamble.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper →
mode-specific push. The rewrite path additionally updates
`refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and returns the new tip SHA.

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature change, no behavioural change, no error-message
  change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` barrel surface is unchanged.
- The helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts`; `src/sync/worktree.ts` stays a
  data-file-agnostic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts`
  (record it as a separate follow-up if it is worth doing).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Risks to keep pinned

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy applied to both paths
  would either publish nothing while reporting success (rewrite) or turn a
  routine no-change sync into an error (incremental). The sibling's
  negative-proof tests fail if this happens.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two messages would drop the
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where
  it does not belong). The hint is an explicit parameter; the exact-text test
  pins it.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }`
  through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path fetches the polluted ref
  again — the exact bug the earlier split fixed.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the
  callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing. The helper's
  generic return must stay honest so the rewrite caller cannot silently drop
  the SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
  - The helper owns: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot`/`getRepoRelativePath`/`path.resolve`, the existence check, `withTempWorktree` + `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync` + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + `commit`.
  - The four documented differences stay explicit options: `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `forceOrphan` (rewrite only), `skipPrePushHint` (incremental only).
  - The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback; the rewrite path still returns the new tip SHA and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
  - Duplicate-block inspection: none of the ten preamble steps appears twice.

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - The sibling's tests (empty-stage, missing-file, refs messages, cross-project guard, push flags) pass unchanged and green after the refactor.
  - `{ forceOrphan: true }` is threaded to `withTempWorktree` on the rewrite path only; the pre-push hint appears on the incremental path only; the rewrite path cannot silently drop the tip SHA.

- **Size and structural gate.** `src/sync/push.ts` shrinks (net fewer lines); no file exceeds 1,000 lines; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` is green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` **unchanged** (no re-baselining); `npm run build` is green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.
  - `src/sync/push.ts` net shorter; no file exceeds 1,000 lines.
  - `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` unchanged (no re-baselining).
  - `npm run build` green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) green.

- **No surface change.** The `src/sync.ts` barrel exports are identical (same names, same signatures — asserted by `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`); no consumer edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.
  - Barrel export names and signatures identical; no edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the `src/sync/push.ts` module header (naming the helper and the two policies) and the `src/sync/push.ts` row/table entry in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if its description changes. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
  - `src/sync/push.ts` module header names the helper and the two mode-specific policies.
  - The `src/sync/push.ts` row in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is updated if the module description changes; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched (release pipeline owns it).

- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
  - Enforced at the dev-push gate (pre-push hook runs `--scope full`).

## Key Files

- `src/sync/push.ts` — new private helper; both public functions rewritten on
  top of it; module header updated.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `withTempWorktree`,
  `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`,
  `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRelativePath`.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `getRemoteTrackingRef` for the
  rewrite path's post-push bookkeeping.
- `src/sync.ts` — Unchanged barrel; verify the exports are identical.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green);
  `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` must not be regenerated.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — update the `src/sync/push.ts` row if the module
  description changes.

# Placement gate false-positive blocks epic driving on a busy machine

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent <epic>` refuses to proceed for an epic child whose
worktree exists but holds no changes whenever **any** other registered
worktree of the repository is dirty:

```
ERROR: Child WL-... produced changes in the sibling worktree
.../worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC... instead of its worktree ...
Offending paths: ...
```

`_child_main_checkout_violation` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`)
treats "child worktree clean + sibling worktree dirty" as evidence that the
child wrote outside its tree. Condition 3 of its documented precision rule
says pre-existing/unrelated dirt must not block a legitimate child, but the
code only earns that exemption when the child's own worktree already holds
changes — which a **freshly started child never does**. The result: on a
machine running several concurrent dispatches (the normal steady state),
`parent` and `drive` fail closed before the first child session is ever
spawned.

## Evidence (captured 2026-11-18, parent epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9)

1. `implement.py parent WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` started child
   WL-0MWKY141H002LULI and created its (empty) worktree.
2. `implement.py drive WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` then failed in `phase_parent`
   with one message per dirty sibling worktree:
   - `wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG-...` (item soft-deleted, 3 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MVOBP8MC0093Y7T-...` (blocked item, 22 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV-...` (live concurrent dispatch, 15 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWMGEL5R003IH71-...` (6 dirty paths)
   - `/tmp/wl-base-check`, `/tmp/wl-clean-check`, ... (1 dirty path each)
   `sessions_spawned: 0` — no child session ran, so no child work existed.
3. Removing the empty worktree (`implement.py abort`) and re-running `drive`
   let the chain start normally: `phase_start` recreated the tree and the
   session was spawned, precisely because no clean worktree existed at the
   moment the placement check ran.

## Desired change

A freshly started child (worktree created, no session spawned against it yet)
must never be reported as a placement violation because of dirt in a
*different* work item's worktree. Candidate treatments, in order of
preference:

- Exempt a child whose worktree was created by this run's `phase_start` and
  has never had a session spawned against it (the same shape as the existing
  `read_spawn_failure` exemption).
- Restrict the sibling scan to worktrees whose dirt this child's session could
  have produced (age ordering vs the child worktree creation time).
- At minimum, fail-open (WARNING) when the offending sibling belongs to an
  independently live, non-terminal item (a concurrent dispatch), keeping the
  hard failure only for siblings whose item is terminal (deleted/completed),
  where the dirt genuinely is orphaned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test drives `phase_parent`/`_child_main_checkout_violation` with a
  clean child worktree and at least one dirty sibling worktree owned by a
  distinct non-terminal item and asserts the child is reported startable, not
  failed.
- A second test pins the genuine case that must stay fail-closed: dirt in a
  sibling worktree attributable to this child's own session still fails
  placement.
- `implement.py drive <epic>` completes its first `parent` step and spawns the
  first child session on a repository where other items' worktrees are dirty.
- No existing placement/attribution test regresses.

## Impact

An epic can be driven on a machine that is also running other dispatches,
instead of the driver dead-ending before the first child session.

Discovered from WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 (deps: discovered-from:WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9).

**Key Files:**

# ruff DTZ007: naive datetime in `_job_elapsed_seconds` (rss_server.py:2856-2857)

## Problem

Ruff reports DTZ007 — "Naive datetime constructed using `datetime.datetime.strptime()` without `%z`" — on two adjacent lines in `rss_server.py` (`_job_elapsed_seconds` function). The function parses `created_at` / `updated_at` ISO-8601 UTC timestamps to compute wall-clock elapsed seconds. Both datetimes are naive but represent the same UTC epoch, so the subtraction produces correct elapsed seconds. However, the code is inconsistent with the project's broader use of tz-aware datetimes.

## Users

- **Producer / audit system**: needs a consistent decision on whether this narrow, safe pattern is accepted as a false positive (record waiver) or fixed.
- **Future maintainers**: would benefit from consistent datetime handling (tz-aware throughout).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Producer accepts one of two paths:
   - **Option A — Accept as false positive:** Record an audit waiver via `audit_waiver.py add <audited-item-id> --rule DTZ007 --file src/rss_server.py --justification "…"`. A waiver with no `--line` would cover both lines (2856 and 2857) and prevents re-creation of chores.
   - **Option B — Fix the code:** Replace `strptime` with tz-aware parsing (preferred: `.fromisoformat(dt_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))` consistent with existing pattern at line 2216) **or** add `.replace(tzinfo=UTC)` post-parse.
2. If Option B is chosen, apply the same fix to the sibling work item for line 2856 (WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP), or combine into a single fix.
3. The ruff check `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py` passes (zero errors) after resolution.

## Impact

Ruff DTZ007 false-positive decision: accept the narrow elapsed-time pattern as a waiver (no code change) or fix the two datetime parses to use tz-aware ISO timestamps, improving consistency with the rest of the project.

## Constraints

- The fix must not change the function's return value (elapsed seconds in float).
- If fixing, the approach must be consistent with the project's existing datetime handling pattern (see line 2216).
- The sibling item (line 2856) shares the same function and should be resolved in the same change.

## Existing state

- Function `_job_elapsed_seconds(job: dict) -> float | None` at line 2845 parses `created_at`/`updated_at` as naive UTC datetimes via `strptime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")` and returns `(ended - started).total_seconds()`.
- The project imports `from datetime import UTC, datetime` and uses `datetime.now(UTC)` and `datetime.fromisoformat(dt_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))` elsewhere.
- Sibling work item WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP (line 2856) — both lines in the same function, same root cause.

## Key Files

- `src/rss_server.py` — `_job_elapsed_seconds` function (lines 2845–2859)

- WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP — ruff DTZ007 at line 2856 (same function, sibling finding).
- Line 2216 in `rss_server.py` — existing pattern `dt_str.replace("Z", "+00:00")` / `datetime.fromisoformat(dt_str)` — candidate for reuse.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The sibling line 2856 item exists separately; should be resolved in the same change but tracked as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** The timestamps are always in the same UTC format; no cross-timezone edge cases.
- **Assumption:** The audit waiver mechanism records on the audited work item (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8), not this chore — the `audit_waiver.py add` command targets the correct item.

## Description

`wl delete` runs an auto-sync after a successful mutation, but the internal `performSync` call does **not** forward the project's `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list (nor the derived `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()`. The author-identity gate therefore runs in strict mode and refuses any incoming commit whose author is not the local `user.email` — even when the project explicitly allow-lists that identity for `wl sync`.

**Root cause:** `src/commands/delete.ts` (~line 298) builds the `performSync` options from `getSyncDefaults()` but only passes `gitRemote` and `gitBranch`, dropping `allowedAuthors` and `allowForeignAuthor`. The CLI `wl sync` command (`src/commands/sync.ts` ~line 800-834) correctly forwards both, which is why explicit syncs honour the allow-list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl delete` auto-sync forwards `allowedAuthors` (and `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()` into `performSync`, so a commit authored by an allow-listed identity merges without refusal.
- Strict mode is preserved: when the config has no allow-list (or `syncAllowedAuthors: []`), a foreign-author commit is still refused by delete auto-sync, and the existing warning is still printed on refusal.
- The empty-author-email gate is unchanged: an allow-list can never admit an empty author.
- The "sync failure must not abort the delete" contract is preserved: a genuine refusal still warns and leaves the local mutation intact.
- `--no-sync` still skips the auto-sync entirely.
- The delete regression tests (`tests/cli/delete-auto-sync-allow-list.test.ts`) pass.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` option contract is unchanged (no breaking change to the CLI sync path).

In `src/commands/delete.ts`, in the auto-sync block:

```ts
const defaults = getSyncDefaults(config || undefined);
await performSync(dataPath, utils.getDatabase, {
  file: dataPath,
  prefix: options.prefix,
  gitRemote: defaults.gitRemote,
  gitBranch: defaults.gitBranch,
  allowedAuthors: defaults.allowedAuthors,        // <-- add
  allowForeignAuthor: defaults.allowForeignAuthor, // <-- add
  push: true,
  dryRun: false,
  silent: true,
  isJsonMode,
  isVerbose: false,
});
```

`performSync` already accepts both fields in its options interface (`src/commands/sync.ts` lines 76-77).

- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `getSyncDefaults()` and `performSync` options interface

## Goal

Provide the **read side** of the repeatable producer-review provenance audit: one injectable, strictly read-only seam that turns a worklog root into everything `classifyProducerReviewProvenance` needs for that root's flagged prep set.

Child 1 of 4 of WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD). It is the acquisition half only; classification/assembly is child 2 and the command surface is child 3.

## User story

As a remediation agent, I want comments, the stored audit record and dependency edges for the flagged prep set read through one injectable seam, so that the audit cannot re-implement the read side (which is where the edge direction was got wrong in the 2026-11-23 audit).

## Context

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts` already owns the read pattern to copy: `createPrepSupplyReportDeps()` wires `wl worklist --json`, a per-root `wl list --json` fallback per prep stage, batched in-process dependency edges with a per-item `wl dep list --json` fallback, and the rolling dispatch log. Its header documents the read-only contract.
- That seam has **no comment and no stored-audit read**. Confirmed payload shapes:
  - `wl show <id> --json` returns `{ success, workItem, comments, auditResult, auditWaiver }` — `comments[]` carry `{ id, workItemId, author, comment, createdAt, references }`.
  - `wl audit-show <id> --json` returns `{ success, workItemId, audit: null }` or `{ success, workItemId, audit: { readyToClose, auditedAt, summary, rawOutput, author, fingerprint } }`.
- `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (`downtime-worker.parsers.ts`) keeps only `direction === 'depends-on'` (outbound) edges — the exact predicate that prevents the inbound `depended-on-by` misread.
- `PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts`) is `['idea', 'intake_complete']` and must be reused, not redefined.
- Per-item reads are acceptable because the bound is the flagged prep set (18 rows across four roots in the 2026-11-23 audit); the seam must not fan out to every prep item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new read-only source module, sibling to `downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts`, exposes an injectable seam that returns per root: the flagged prep set, per-item comments, per-item stored audit record, outbound dependency blocker refs and the rolling dispatch-log entries.
- The flagged set is read with `wl list --json --needs-producer-review --include-not-started` and filtered to `PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES` (the constant is imported, never redefined).
- Comments are mapped from `wl show <id> --json` `comments[]` onto `ProducerReviewComment` and the stored record from `wl audit-show <id> --json` `audit` onto `ProducerReviewAuditRecord` (`audit: null` maps to "no stored record", not an error).
- Dependency edges are read through the existing batched in-process reader with the per-item `wl dep list --json` fallback and filtered by `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, so only outbound `depends-on` edges survive.
- A malformed or unparseable payload for a root is surfaced as that root's error (fail-closed) and named; it is never rendered as an empty, healthy set, while other roots still read.
- Strictly read-only: no flag, assignee or marker mutation (regression test). Write surfaces are injected to throw if called, and the dispatch-log file bytes are asserted unchanged after a run.
- Tests are written first and cover: flagged-set parsing, `wl show` comment parsing, `audit-show` null and record parsing, outbound-only edge filtering, and fail-closed on malformed JSON.

## Goal

Provide the **pure assembly half** of the repeatable producer-review provenance audit: turn the read seam's per-item data into provenance rows whose `holds` are computed from the dispatcher's own gate predicates over **outbound** `depends-on` edges only.

Child 2 of 4 of WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD). It fills the one seam the existing rule left open: `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput.holds` is already accepted but nothing populates it.

## User story

As a remediation agent, I want the `can-clear-now` set to come from the dispatcher's own predicates, so that the flags I clear are provably safe to clear and the inbound-`depended-on-by` misread of the 2026-11-23 audit cannot recur.

## Context

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` already implements the rule as pure functions: `classifyProducerReviewProvenance(input)` (plain data in, verdict out) and `assembleProducerReviewProvenance(rows)` (id-sorted rows + groups). It must be **reused unchanged**; this child only fills `holds` and adds `root`.
- The hold vocabulary is `dependency`, `assignee-hold`, `startOn`, `attempt-budget`, `cooldown`, `dispatch-marker`.
- Predicates to reuse, never restate: `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`, gates `assignee-hold` / `startOnNotReached` / `not-dispatchable`), `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`), `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` and `dispatchedItemMarkers` / `markerStillExcludes` (`downtime-log-markers.ts`), `prepSupplyKindForStage` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts`), and the outbound-only edge predicate (`TERMINAL_STATUSES` semantics: an unresolvable or non-terminal blocker is unmet).
- **Critical subtlety:** `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` returns `producer-review` first when `needsProducerReview === true`, and every audited item carries that flag. The holds derivation must therefore call it with `needsProducerReview` masked to `false` (never mutating the item), or the assignee/`startOn` holds would never be observed.

# Drive placement guard false-positives on a sibling item's mid-flight worktree after a transient provider failure

## Problem statement

When an epic child's first session dies on a transient provider error, `implement.py drive` correctly classifies the failure as `infrastructure` and records an infra-retry, but it does **not** record spawn-failure evidence before re-running the parent phase. The re-run parent phase therefore sees a clean child worktree (no work of its own) plus a *live* sibling worktree holding commits ahead of `dev`, and `_child_main_checkout_violation` attributes that sibling's work to the failed child — stopping the whole drive chain with a false accusation against an unrelated item.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher / drive operator** — needs epic drives to survive a transient provider hiccup without manual intervention.
- **Work-item producer** — needs the placement guard to accuse the right item only; a false positive on a live sibling is misleading and costly.

Example user stories:

- As the downtime dispatcher, a driven epic child whose first session dies on a transient provider error is retried instead of having the whole drive chain stopped by a placement violation naming an unrelated worktree.
- As a producer, I can trust a `placement_violation` refusal to mean a child genuinely wrote outside its worktree, not that another item happened to be mid-flight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A child whose session failure was classified `infrastructure` is exempt from `_child_main_checkout_violation` from the moment of that failure (either record spawn-failure evidence before the retry `continue`, or pass the driver's reconciliation verdict into the parent-phase guard).
- Regression test: a driven child that fails with an `infrastructure` verdict while a *live* sibling worktree holds commits ahead of `dev` and the child's own worktree is clean → no placement violation; the retry proceeds.
- Regression test unchanged: a child that genuinely wrote into a sibling worktree (no failure evidence) still fails closed with the existing message.
- No weakening for the `CHILD_DIRTY`/`CHILD_AHEAD` cases: a child that produced its own work never reaches the exemption.

## Impact

Epic drives keep running through a transient provider error instead of stopping with a false accusation against another item's worktree.

## Constraints

- The fix must stay inside `_child_main_checkout_violation` and its `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` callers; no unrelated guard behaviour changes.
- The existing placement/attribution precision rule (conditions 1–3) and every existing exemption/message must be preserved.
- Genuine cross-worktree-write detection (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I) must remain intact: a child that produced work never earns the exemption.
- The infra-retry budget (`--infra-retry-limit`) and per-child session bound accounting must not change.

## Existing state

- `_child_main_checkout_violation` (in `implement.py`, ~L21184) returns early when the child's own worktree holds work (condition 3), then exempts a child only when `read_spawn_failure()` finds `<worktree>/.worklog/spawn-failure.json`.
- `record_spawn_failure()` is called **only after** the infra-retry budget is exhausted (the "A classified infrastructure failure that reaches here has spent the shared budget" branch, ~L20600+). The infra-retry path records nothing and `continue`s the retry loop.
- Consequently, on the immediately re-run parent phase, the failed child carries no spawn-failure evidence, its own worktree is clean, and a live sibling worktree (e.g. `wl-WL-0MWW355UL0038DDI-...` holding commit `ea549e293`) is treated as the child's foreign write surface.
- The occurrence is documented in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` → **The placement guard** (spawn-failure exemption paragraph, SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G) which describes the exemption as if it always applies after a failed session — it does not cover the mid-retry window.

## Desired change

Make the infrastructure-classification exemption apply from the moment the driver classifies the failure, so the immediately re-run parent phase treats the child as startable rather than as a stray writer. Candidate treatments, in order of preference:

1. **Record spawn-failure evidence before the retry `continue`** — call `record_spawn_failure(...)` (guarded by `_classify_child_worktree(...) in (CHILD_CLEAN, CHILD_NO_WORK)`, as the exhausted-budget path already does) on the infra-retry path, so the existing `read_spawn_failure()` exemption covers the window with no new plumbing.
2. **Pass the driver's reconciliation verdict into the parent-phase guard** — thread the `infrastructure` classification into `_child_main_checkout_violation` as an explicit "this child produced no work" signal.

Option 1 reuses the existing exemption mechanism and needs no signature change; it is the preferred treatment unless implementation reveals a reason the record cannot be written before the retry.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation` (~L21184), `record_spawn_failure`/`read_spawn_failure` (~L11898/~L11961), the infra-retry `continue` path (~L20590) and the budget-exhausted `record_spawn_failure` call (~L20618).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing stray-write, spawn-failure-evidence and infra-retry coverage (`TestDrivenChildStraysIntoSiblingWorktree`, `TestSpawnFailureEvidence`, `TestDriveRetriesProviderStreamFailure`); add the new regression tests here.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_spawn_failure_classification.py` — provider-failure classification pinned here; the new tests build on the same classification.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — **The placement guard** section documents the spawn-failure exemption; update to note the exemption applies from the moment of an `infrastructure` classification, not only after the retry budget is spent.

## Related work

- WL-0MWMMYW9H009YAJV — "implement.py refuses an epic child when any sibling worktree is dirty" (in-progress in this store; judged misfiled and deleted as duplicate of SA-0MWL0XX88000E38K in SorraAgents). Same `_child_main_checkout_violation` precision-rule area (fresh/clean child + dirty sibling); no AC overlap with this item's *transient-failure* attribution gap.
- WL-0MWMOP4H8007T9GG — test: fresh child + dirty sibling false positive (open, sibling epic child).
- WL-0MWMOQ5A8000M4W5 — fix `_child_main_checkout_violation` to exempt fresh child (open, sibling epic child).
- WL-0MWQLHDOS006CAIH — "Stale scratch worktrees make the implement foreign-change-surface guard refuse clean children" (completed) — introduced the live-foreign-surface debris filter; this item is the transient-failure analogue.
- WL-0MWQM8JPV001WIMY — "Implement live foreign surface filter in implement.py" (completed) — live-surface filter implementation; unaffected here.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the driver can classify the failure as `infrastructure` and read `_classify_child_worktree(...)` before the retry `continue` — both values are already computed on that path.
- **Risk (regression):** writing spawn-failure evidence on the retry path could exempt a child that later genuinely strays on a subsequent attempt. **Mitigation:** `phase_start` calls `clear_spawn_failure`, so a re-spawned session starts with no stale record; the new record is written only for `CHILD_CLEAN`/`CHILD_NO_WORK`, so a session that produced work never earns it.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the sibling item WL-0MWMMYW9H009YAJV covers the adjacent fresh-child/dirty-sibling false positive; resist folding that general precision-rule work into this item. Record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Failure mode if unfixed:** every epic drive that coincides with another item mid-flight in a sibling worktree is stopped dead by a transient provider hiccup the child did not cause.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which implementation treatment should be used — record spawn-failure evidence before the retry `continue`, or thread the driver's reconciliation verdict into `_child_main_checkout_violation`?
  **Answer (agent, reasonable assumption):** Prefer recording spawn-failure evidence before the retry `continue` (Option 1). It reuses the established `read_spawn_failure()` exemption and the existing `_classify_child_worktree(...) in (CHILD_CLEAN, CHILD_NO_WORK)` guard, requires no signature change to the guard, and keeps the genuine-stray detection intact. Evidence: `implement.py` ~L20600–20623 (the exhausted-budget path already uses exactly this pattern). No producer decision required — the item's AC1 explicitly permits either treatment.
- **Q:** Does the existing stray-write regression suite already cover a clean child with no failure evidence against a dirty sibling? 
  **Answer (research):** Yes — `test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py::TestDrivenChildStraysIntoSiblingWorktree` pins the fail-closed genuine case, and `TestSpawnFailureEvidence` pins the record round-trip. `TestDriveRetriesProviderStreamFailure` exercises the infra-retry accounting but uses a stub `_parent`, so it does not go through `_child_main_checkout_violation`. Source: inspected the test module (L182–L1580).
